text: [clean] Start by identifying the object type and its likely locations based on common usage or storage.
[clean] Always check the most probable locations first, such as sinks, countertops, cabinets, or drawers.
[clean] Open containers (e.g., cabinets, drawers, fridges) before searching inside them.
[clean] Clean the object using a sinkbasin as soon as it is retrieved.
[clean] After cleaning, place the object in the specified target location, starting with the most accessible or logical one.
[clean] If the object is not found in expected locations, systematically check all remaining possibilities.
[cool] Search for the object in likely locations such as stoveburners, countertops, diningtables, cabinets, or drawers, starting with the most probable.
[cool] Cool the object using the fridge after it has been picked up.
[cool] Always open the fridge before attempting to cool an object.
[cool] Place the cooled object in the specified target location (e.g., diningtable, garbagecan, sidetable) after cooling.
[cool] If an object is not found in initial locations, systematically check all possible storage areas.
[cool] Avoid redundant checks by progressing to the next location if the current one does not contain the desired object.
[examine] Start by identifying the target object and the tool needed to examine it.
[examine] Systematically check likely locations for the target object, starting with the most probable ones.
[examine] Open or interact with containers (drawers, cabinets, etc.) to access hidden items.
[examine] Once the target object is found, locate and use the examination tool (e.g., desklamp) to complete the task.
[examine] If the task involves "under the desklamp," ensure the desklamp is turned on and check the area it illuminates.
[examine] Re-examine areas if the task is not yet complete, especially if the object might be hidden or overlooked.
[heat] Check common storage locations first (fridge, countertop, diningtable) when searching for food items.
[heat] Open containers (e.g., fridge, microwave, cabinet) before inspecting or using their contents.
[heat] Use the microwave to heat the object after it has been retrieved.
[heat] Always confirm the object is in hand before attempting to heat or move it.
[heat] Place the heated object in the specified target location as instructed in the task.
[heat] Prioritize checking high-probability locations based on object type (e.g., mugs in cabinets or countertops).
[put] Check cabinets, drawers, and countertops first when searching for small objects like pencils, candles, or books.
[put] If the object is not in storage units, search sidetables, shelves, and surfaces like coffee tables or dining tables.
[put] Always open closed containers before inspecting their contents.
[put] Once the object is found, directly move it to the target location without unnecessary intermediate steps.
[put] Prioritize locations based on object type (e.g., remote controls on tables, books on sidetables or dressers).
[put] If the object is not in expected storage, systematically check all visible surfaces and furniture.
[puttwo] Start by systematically checking likely object locations such as drawers, shelves, and tables.
[puttwo] If the first object is found, immediately move it to the target location before searching for the second.
[puttwo] After placing the first object, return to the original location if the second object is still there.
[puttwo] If the second object is not immediately visible, re-examine or revisit previously checked locations.
[puttwo] Prioritize locations where the first object was found when searching for the second.
[puttwo] Use "take" and "put" commands directly with object names once they are identified.
